subject.title: [Bug]: exec-policy can retain a partial approvals update after config failure

question: Should the active approval-race PR absorb this rollback-compensation fix before landing, or should landing wait for a separate focused fix?
rationale: The missing behavior affects persisted execution authorization, while the active PR owns the transaction seam but is already broad and merge-sensitive; the landing boundary requires explicit maintainer judgment.

options.title: Fix in active PR
options.body: Add field-aware compensation and the focused rollback regressions to the existing locked-transaction PR before it lands.

options.title: Block on focused follow-up
options.body: Keep this issue as a required blocker and wait to land the active PR until a focused compensation PR is ready.

options.title: Accept temporary gap
options.body: Land the broader race hardening while explicitly accepting that failed exec-policy config writes can still retain partial approval defaults.

recommendation.title: Fix in active PR
recommendation.body: Add field-aware compensation and the focused rollback regressions to the existing locked-transaction PR before it lands.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the active transaction branch, have the strongest recent history on the approvals implementation, and are assigned to this issue.
